'''John Sarli''' is a [[mathematician]] and [[Academic staff|academic]]. He is a [[Emeritus professor|Professor Emeritus]] of mathematics at [[California State University, San Bernardino|California State University at San Bernardino]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://catalog.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/natural-sciences/mathematics/#faculty|title=Department of Mathematics}}</ref>

Sarli's research focuses on the geometry of [[Group of Lie type|groups of Lie type]] and the applications of [[hyperbolic geometry]]<ref name=ssqer/> with his work published in ''[[Geometriae Dedicata]]'', ''[[Journal of Geometry]]'', ''[[Advances in Geometry]]'', and the ''[[Journal of Elasticity]]''.

==Education==
In 1974, Sarli earned an [[Bachelor of Arts|A.B.]] in [[Mathematics]] from [[Brown University]]. He then pursued advanced studies and received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in Mathematics from the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]] in 1984.<ref name=ssqer>{{cite web|url=https://mdtp.ucsd.edu/about/workgroup/Professional%20Biographies/sarli-john-bio.html|title=John Sarli}}</ref>

==Career==
Sarli was Chair of the Department of Mathematics at California State University, [[San Bernardino, California|San Bernardino]] from 1988 to 1994. In 1999, he joined the Mathematics Diagnostic Testing Project (MDTP) Workgroup. The following year, he took on the role of site director at CSU San Bernardino when an MDTP site was set up there. He assumed the position of Chair of the MDTP Workgroup in 2002 and held the role until 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mdtp.ucsd.edu/about/workgroup/index.html|title=The MDTP Workgroup}}</ref> He holds the title of professor emeritus of Mathematics at California State University, San Bernardino.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.csusb.edu/mathematics/faculty-staff|title=Department of Mathematics Faculty & Staff}}</ref>

==Research==
Sarli, through his research, described an incidence structure for twisted groups 𝐺, where points are [[Elementary abelian group|elementary abelian root subgroups]] establishing a correspondence between certain lines and planes in this structure, demonstrating that it induces a polarity on an embedded [[metasymplectic space]]. He showed that [[Biharmonic equation|biharmonic functions]], crucial for understanding equilibrium equations for elastic bodies, can be derived from a power series using [[matrix representation]]s of 𝐶 and applied to describe solutions to planar equilibrium equations within [[Möbius plane]] geometry.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pascal-francis.inist.fr/vibad/index.php?action=getRecordDetail&idt=3810337|title=Representations of C, biharmonic vector fields, and the equilibrium equation of planar elasticity}}</ref> His alignment of the geometry of root subgroups in 𝐺=PSp<sub>4</sub>(𝑞) with a [[Conic section|system of conics]] in the associated [[generalized quadrangle]] provided an interpretation of symplectic 2-transvections.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://openurl.ebsco.com/EPDB%3Agcd%3A16%3A2307008/detailv2?sid=ebsco%3Aplink%3Ascholar&id=ebsco%3Agcd%3A8944573&crl=c|title=A rank 3 tangent complex of PSp4 (q), q odd.}}</ref> Classifying the intrinsic conics in the hyperbolic plane, using [[collineation]] invariants, he offered [[Metric space|metric characterizations]] and highlighted a natural duality among these classes, induced by an involution related to complementary angles of [[Parallel (geometry)|parallelism]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Sarli |first1=John |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00022-012-0115-5|title=Conics in the hyperbolic plane intrinsic to the collineation group |journal=Journal of Geometry |date=2012 |volume=103 |pages=131–148 |doi=10.1007/s00022-012-0115-5 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Selected articles==
*Sarli, J. (1988). The geometry of root subgroups in Ree groups of type 2 F 4. Geometriae Dedicata, 26(1), 1-28. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00148014
*Sarli, J., & Torner, J. (1993). Representations of <math>\mathbb{C}</math>, biharmonic vector fields, and the equilibrium equation of planar elasticity. Journal of Elasticity, 32(3), 223–241. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF0013166
*Sarli, J., & McClurg, P. (2001). McClurg, P. (2001). A rank 3 tangent complex of 𝑃Sp4(𝑞), 𝑞 odd. Advances in Geometry, 1(4), 365–371. https://doi.org/10.1515/advg.2001.022
*Sarli, J. (2012). Conics in the hyperbolic plane intrinsic to the collineation group. Journal of Geometry, 103, 131–148. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00022-012-0115-5
